finding: Direct owning-host telemetry now resolves an important part of the post-stop drift hypothesis. Two live bash processes with command line tools/run_6000_free_swarm_supervisor.sh (PIDs 680904 and 680982) were observed at both 2026-08-25T22:49:41.466428Z and 2026-08-25T22:50:49.709962Z. The host ps clock is UTC and both processes report START=11:28, whereas the hard-disable commit 34cde26849a31b852b677a38f2c426c75d881bcf was committed at 2026-08-25T19:13:49Z. These are therefore directly observed pre-stop runtime incarnations, not invocations of the current five-line kill-only supervisor source. Historical source at parent 686d1f5c08c956aa6baea8cc8f160c03ab766f9e shows that the pre-stop supervisor ran a 15-second reconciliation loop and could start run_6000_free_swarm_fast.py through free_swarm_exec_with_vault.py when its then-current admission checks passed. This materially strengthens the stale-runtime/source-epoch explanation for post-stop provider-attempt telemetry, while not yet proving that either surviving shell caused each individual OpenRouter counter increment.

hypothesis_update.prior: Post-stop request drift was consistent with stale/unsynchronized runtime authority bytes or another provider-capable path.
hypothesis_update.current: At least two directly observed pre-stop supervisor runtime incarnations survived long after the hard-stop source commit. Because their historical source was provider-capable and recurrent, they are concrete candidate roots for the stale-runtime drift.

counterhypotheses_remaining: The two surviving supervisor shells may be idle with respect to provider calls while a different provider-capable process owns the OpenRouter attempt increments.
A ps command line plus start time identifies process class/incarnation but does not by itself attest the exact script bytes mapped/interpreted by the already-running bash process.
Short-lived descendants may be the actual network callers and can disappear between one-minute telemetry snapshots.
Recorded provider-attempt counters and exact token-usage counters cover different evidence surfaces; a token-usage plateau does not negate failed request-attempt drift.
